type: offline reanalysis of existing closed-loop logs, CPU only, no new rollouts
question: Does the principle 'a stall is evidence of a wrong mode only when a local corrector is active' hold across different correctors, and is a corrector's effect on right-mode success carried by the stall rate (the stall is the channel)?

sets_primary.ER3: Q400ER3 (|residual rz| x sign from error head)

sets_note: All primary sets: Q400 ensemble, same block rule (--evid-k 999 --evid-suppress --evid-fallback 2), stall 3 mm, seeds 20260921/22/23, cohorts 76700..76875, 600 scenes each, same scenes across sets.

definitions.stall: first step with 24-step net hand displacement < 3 mm before min(first success, first 90 deg plug rotation); identical to resoff3_20261119/analyze.py
definitions.TPR: share of flip scenes with a stall
definitions.FPR: share of non-flip scenes with a stall
definitions.AUROC: rank AUROC of -first_stall_step for flip vs non-flip, as resoff3
definitions.mediation: non-flip scenes only. For arm a: p1 = P(success | no stall), p0 = P(success | stall) estimated from the OTHER primary arms pooled (leave-one-arm-out); predicted non-flip success rate of a = p1*(1-FPR_a) + p0*FPR_a; error = predicted - actual.

predictions.G1: TPR >= 0.95 in all five primary sets (a corrector does not remove wrong-mode stalls)
predictions.G2: for each corrector-on set x: FPR(OFF) - FPR(x) >= 0.30 and AUROC(x) >= AUROC(OFF) + 0.15
predictions.G3: mediation error |predicted - actual| <= 0.05 for all four corrector-on sets
predictions.G4: mediation error <= 0.05 for OFF, predicted from the four corrector-on sets only
predictions.G5_reported_only: Spearman of AUROC vs total success across the five sets (n=5, no threshold)

verdict.SUPPORTED: G1 and G2 and G3 and G4
verdict.PARTIAL: G1 and G2 hold, G3 or G4 fails (principle holds across correctors; the stall is not the only channel)

already_known: RES and OFF TPR/FPR/AUROC and success (resoff3: TPR 1.0, FPR 0.30 vs 0.898, AUROC 0.871 vs 0.572, 475 vs 213); total success of B2 523, ER3 525, DZ 498. Not known to me at freeze time: TPR/FPR/AUROC of B2, ER3, DZ; any conditional success rates.
limits: B2 and DZ differ from RES mainly after the first switch, so their pre-switch stall rates may be close to RES: the five sets may give only 2-3 distinct corrector qualities. Sets differ in corrector only, but success after a stall also depends on what the corrector does after the switch, which is why G3/G4 can fail. Simulation, one task. Sim scene outcomes flip in ~11% of scenes under 1e-8 perturbations.
consequence: SUPPORTED: one paper figure (stall rate vs right-mode success across correctors) and the 'stall is the channel' sentence. PARTIAL: report the across-corrector table only. NOT_SUPPORTED: recorded as is; the principle is claimed only for the deployed corrector.
